## Purpose and Entry Points
Gas City is a Go-based orchestration toolkit for multi-agent coding workflows. The primary executable is `gc`, whose root command wires CLI commands, city discovery, configuration, storage, runtimes, and controller behavior. `gc init` scaffolds a city; `gc start` launches its control plane; operational commands manage rigs, work, sessions, formulas, orders, and services.
- `cmd/gc/main.go`
- `cmd/gc/cmd_commands.go`
- `cmd/gc/cmd_start.go`

## City Configuration, Packs, and Scoping
A city is declaratively configured through `city.toml`; configuration composition resolves packs, imports, overlays, provider definitions, storage bindings, agents, named sessions, and rig-specific overrides. Packs are both a distribution boundary and an extensibility mechanism: the embedded core pack supplies default agents, formulas, orders, scripts, skills, and provider overlays.
- `internal/config/config.go`
- `internal/config/compose.go`
- `internal/bootstrap/packs/core/pack.toml`

## Storage and Work Model
“Beads” are the durable work/coordination records underlying work tracking, mail, convoys, waits, and workflow graphs. The store abstraction supports multiple backends, notably the default external `bd`/Dolt path, native Dolt, SQLite, file, and memory implementations. Store binding resolves which backend serves each storage class and protects migrations/lifecycle transitions; this is a major boundary between orchestration logic and persistence.
- `internal/beads/beads.go`
- `internal/beads/factory.go`
- `internal/storebinding/storebinding.go`

## Controller Reconciliation and Dispatch
The controller continuously reconciles configured and observed state into desired pools/sessions. It computes demand, creates or wakes capacity, routes ready work, tracks assignments, and repairs drift or failed ownership. Dispatch turns bead/workflow graph state into runnable work and supports retry, drain, fanout, and control-routing semantics. Conditional writes, residency, and store fences protect cross-process and cross-store ownership.
- `cmd/gc/controller.go`
- `cmd/gc/build_desired_state.go`
- `cmd/gc/session_reconciler.go`
- `internal/dispatch/runtime.go`

## Sessions, Workers, and Runtime Providers
Sessions are the lifecycle unit for an agent invocation: identity, persisted state, waits, chat/submission, transcript metadata, and transitions are handled independently of a concrete runtime. Worker handles normalize agent operations and observation. The runtime interface permits the same orchestration layer to launch or control tmux, local subprocess/exec, ACP, Kubernetes, SSH, hybrid, T3 bridge, or herdr providers. tmux remains the default/fallback runtime.
- `internal/session/manager.go`
- `internal/worker/handle.go`
- `internal/runtime/runtime.go`
- `internal/runtime/tmux/tmux.go`
- `internal/runtime/k8s/provider.go`

## Workflow Compilation and Scheduled Automation
Formulas define reusable multi-step workflows and compile into graph-shaped molecule/work records. The convergence subsystem runs bounded iterative refinement and gates over those workflows. Orders are separately parsed periodic or event-triggered automation definitions; their dispatcher evaluates triggers and launches actions through the same control/runtime boundaries.
- `internal/formula/compile.go`
- `internal/molecule/molecule.go`
- `internal/convergence/reconcile.go`
- `internal/orders/triggers.go`

## Supervisor, API, Observability, and Integrations
A supervisor manages city-level service lifecycle, publishes status, and can host the HTTP control API and embedded dashboard. The API exposes typed resources for cities, sessions, agents, beads, runs, events, mail, rigs, and operational actions; SSE supports live streams. Events provide durable observability, while external-message and webhook modules connect outside systems. Optional infrastructure includes managed Dolt, Git/GitHub, MCP mail, Docker, and Kubernetes manifests.
- `internal/supervisor/registry.go`
- `internal/api/server.go`
- `internal/api/dashboardspa/embed.go`
- `internal/events/events.go`
- `internal/extmsg/services.go`
